subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a low-level language?
options: Python
Java
Assembly language
C#
questions.explain: Assembly language is a low-level language that uses mnemonics closely tied to the processor's instruction set.

questions.q: In which form is machine code expressed?
options: Binary
Denary
Hexadecimal mnemonics
Natural English
questions.explain: Machine code is the lowest-level language and is written in binary (1s and 0s) that the CPU executes directly.

questions.q: Assembly language uses short abbreviations, such as ADD and MOV, that represent machine instructions. What are these abbreviations called?
options: Keywords
Mnemonics
Operands
Comments
questions.explain: Assembly language uses mnemonics, which are memorable abbreviations that each correspond to a machine code instruction.

questions.q: Which statement about high-level languages is correct?
options: They can be executed directly by the CPU without translation
One statement typically translates into many machine code instructions
They are specific to one type of processor
They are written using binary op-codes
questions.explain: A single high-level statement usually expands into many machine code instructions when translated.

questions.q: Why is a program written in a high-level language generally easier to write and debug than one written in machine code?
options: It runs faster on every processor
Its syntax is closer to natural human language
It never needs to be translated
It uses less memory than machine code
questions.explain: High-level languages use English-like keywords and structures, making them easier for people to read, write and debug.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of a high-level language over a low-level language?
options: It gives more direct control over specific hardware
It is portable and can run on different types of machine after translation
It always produces a smaller, faster program
It does not require any translator
questions.explain: High-level code is largely portable because it is not tied to one processor, unlike machine-specific low-level code.

questions.q: A programmer needs to write code that controls hardware directly and makes the most efficient use of the processor's resources. Which type of language is best suited to this?
options: A high-level language
A low-level language
A mark-up language
A query language
questions.explain: Low-level languages allow direct control of hardware and efficient use of resources because they map closely to the machine's instructions.

questions.q: What does a compiler do?
options: Translates the whole program into machine code in one go before execution
Translates and executes the program one line at a time
Converts machine code back into high-level source code
Translates assembly language into mnemonics
questions.explain: A compiler translates the entire source program into machine code at once, producing an executable file.

questions.q: How does an interpreter process a program?
options: It translates the whole program before running any of it
It translates and executes the code one line at a time
It converts the code into assembly language only
It produces a permanent executable file
questions.explain: An interpreter translates and runs a program line by line, stopping when it reaches an error.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an assembler?
options: To translate a high-level language into machine code
To translate assembly language into machine code
To translate machine code into a high-level language
To execute an interpreted program
questions.explain: An assembler translates assembly language into machine code, with a one-to-one relationship between the two.

questions.q: Which statement best describes how a compiler and an interpreter report errors?
options: Both report all errors only after the program finishes running
A compiler reports errors at the end of compilation, while an interpreter stops at the first error it meets
An interpreter reports all errors before running, while a compiler ignores errors
Neither can detect syntax errors
questions.explain: A compiler checks the whole program and lists errors after compiling, whereas an interpreter halts at the first error encountered.

questions.q: Why does compiled code typically run faster than the same program being interpreted?
options: Compiled code is stored in binary and interpreted code is not
The translation into machine code is done in advance, so no translation is needed while it runs
Interpreters use more memory than compilers
Compilers remove all comments from the code
questions.explain: A compiled program is already fully translated, so execution is not slowed by translating each line at run time.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of using an interpreter during program development?
options: It produces a faster final executable
It allows code to be tested and errors located line by line as they occur
It hides the source code from the developer
It does not require the interpreter to be installed to run
questions.explain: Interpreters make debugging easier during development because they run code line by line and stop at each error.

questions.q: A company wants to distribute software to customers as an executable file that runs quickly and without revealing the source code. Which translator is most appropriate?
options: An interpreter
A compiler
An assembler
A disassembler
questions.explain: A compiler produces a standalone, fast-running executable and does not distribute the original source code.

questions.q: A student is repeatedly editing and testing small sections of a program and wants immediate feedback on each change. Which translator best suits this way of working?
options: A compiler
An assembler
An interpreter
A linker
questions.explain: An interpreter runs code immediately line by line, giving quick feedback that suits frequent editing and testing.

questions.q: What does 'IDE' stand for?
options: Integrated Development Environment
Internal Data Editor
Interpreted Debugging Engine
Interactive Design Editor
questions.explain: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) provides tools that help a programmer write, test and debug code in one application.

questions.q: In an IDE, what is the purpose of a breakpoint?
options: To permanently delete a line of code
To pause execution at a chosen line so the program's state can be examined
To automatically correct spelling in the code
To translate the code into machine code
questions.explain: A breakpoint halts the program at a set point during debugging so the programmer can inspect variables and flow.

questions.q: How does syntax highlighting in an IDE's editor help a programmer?
options: It runs the program faster
It colours keywords and structures differently to make code easier to read and spot mistakes
It automatically translates the code into binary
It hides all the comments in the code
questions.explain: Syntax highlighting uses colour to distinguish code elements, aiding readability and helping spot errors.

questions.q: Which IDE feature helps a programmer locate and fix logic errors by allowing them to run code line by line and inspect variable values?
options: Auto-completion
Debugging (error diagnostic) tools
Syntax highlighting
A run-time environment
questions.explain: Debugging tools such as stepping, breakpoints and variable watches let programmers trace execution and find errors.

questions.q: A programmer's IDE suggests the full name of a variable after they type only its first few letters. Which IDE feature is being used?
options: Auto-completion
A breakpoint
A translator
Syntax highlighting
questions.explain: Auto-completion predicts and offers to finish identifiers and keywords as they are typed, speeding up coding and reducing typing errors.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Computer Science (J277) specification; Programming Languages & IDEs
